Unsymmetrical bending occurs when flexural members are subjected to transverse
loads acting in a plane other than a principal plane. With this type of loading, the
following are applicable:
The member's neutral axis is not perpendicular to the plane of loading.
Stresses cannot in general be calculated by means of the simple bending
formula (Mc/1).
The bending deflection does not coincide with the plane of loading but is
perpendicular to the inclined neutral axis.
If the plane of loads does not pass through the shear center of the cross
section, bending is also accompanied by twisting.
Doubly-symmetric S, W, and box sections acting as individual beam elements and
subjected to biaxial bending, i.e., unsymmetrical bending without torsion, can be treated
